Class CustomContainerScreen

java.lang.Object
net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.AbstractContainerEventHandler
net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen
net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<CustomContainerMenu>
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.menu.CustomContainerScreen
All Implemented Interfaces:
net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.ContainerEventHandler, net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.GuiEventListener, net.minecraft.client.gui.components.Renderable, net.minecraft.client.gui.components.TabOrderedElement, net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.MenuAccess<CustomContainerMenu>
public class CustomContainerScreen extends net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<CustomContainerMenu>
Client-side partner to CustomContainerMenu: a standalone screen whose panels hold slot groups. Owns hover events, key actions, drag modes and the server's shown flags; placement, render and element input belong to its MenuKit OwnHost, and slot positions to the panels' slot elements.

Its panels

The handler knows each panel's id, slot groups and whether the server shows it; how a panel looks is declared on the client with ClientMenu.panel(String, Consumer) on MenuKit's Panel.Builder, slots included: the mod adds the panel's SlotFlowElement or SlotElements as in any other panel. This screen builds one Panel per handler panel from that declaration (a menu panel with none is an error when the screen opens) and shows it while the server says so.

Its host

The panels go into a standalone host with the title band inside the frame. The host places them by their PanelPosition; an unplaced one takes the standalone default (the first is the main() frame, later ones stack below it). This screen tells the host what it cannot know on its own: a panel's content size, and that the main panel auto-fits its height only when it holds no slots. A panel's own slots stay live under its claim through their elements, as on any screen. The host is attached to MenuKit's screen, so claims and modals see these panels together with anything injected onto it.

Frame order

  1. extractContents HEAD: layout, then the host's FLOW layer (backgrounds, slot frames, elements), under every slot;
  2. vanilla: labels, slot highlight, slots (created slots included);
  3. ContainerScreenLayers: injected FLOW panels, then the dim and every host's OVERLAY layer, this screen's included.

    • captureReturnAction

      public static @Nullable Runnable captureReturnAction()
      A "return to this container" action for the custom container screen now showing, or null if the current screen is not one.

      Use it when opening a temporary client Screen over an open custom container: pass the action to MKScreen.setReturnAction so the temporary screen's Back or Escape opens the container again. It has to reopen rather than just restore the screen on the client, because vanilla closes the server-synced menu when you setScreen away from a container. Coming back means sending the open request again, which is what the returned Runnable does: it finds this menu's CustomMenu handle and calls ClientMenu.requestOpen().

      Returns null when there is nothing to return to (not in a custom container, or the menu's type isn't a registered handle), so callers fall back to their usual navigation. This only restores custom containers; a vanilla container can't be cleanly reopened from the client after the close packet.

    • togglePanel

      public void togglePanel(String panelId)
      Asks the server to show or hide a panel (vanilla's container button packet). The server honors it only for a panel declared toggleable() and the change arrives with the next sync; the client never changes it on its own. Listeners hear onPanelToggle when the server's answer arrives.
